workflow: Maintaining WhatsApp automation by constantly re-pairing devices and re-authenticating sessions after WhatsApp updates break unofficial libraries.
trigger: WhatsApp server-side updates that invalidate existing authentication credentials or change the multi-device protocol.
current_workaround: Developers manually regenerate QR codes, re-link devices, or downgrade library versions to restore functionality. Some maintain multiple fallback accounts.
consequence: Automation downtime for businesses relying on WhatsApp for customer communication, sales, or support. Lost messages, missed leads, and operational overhead.

workflow: Managing rate limits and avoiding number bans by implementing complex throttling, delays, and account rotation strategies.
trigger: Sending messages or making API calls too quickly, triggering WhatsApp's abuse detection.
current_workaround: Developers manually tune delays between messages, implement exponential backoff, rotate between multiple phone numbers, and monitor ban status.
consequence: Permanent or temporary ban of the WhatsApp number, loss of business communication channel, and need to acquire new numbers.

workflow: Implementing message history synchronization from scratch because WhatsApp's multi-device protocol does not expose past messages.
trigger: Business need to access or analyze historical chat data for compliance, customer service, or analytics.
current_workaround: Developers build custom scripts to scrape messages from the phone or use third-party backup extraction tools. Some manually export chats from WhatsApp Desktop.
consequence: Inability to retrieve historical context for customer conversations, loss of data for compliance, and extra development effort.

workflow: Manually managing group participants, sending bulk messages to groups, and handling group metadata because the unofficial libraries lack full group management APIs.
trigger: Business requirement to send announcements to multiple groups, add/remove members, or retrieve group participant lists.
current_workaround: Developers write custom scripts using low-level protocol commands or use multiple library versions to cover different group operations.
consequence: Incomplete group management, inability to scale group-based communication, and risk of account bans due to unsupported operations.

workflow: Implementing catalog/product message sending and broadcast list management manually because these features are not supported by unofficial libraries.
trigger: Business need to send product catalogs or broadcast messages to multiple contacts for marketing or sales.
current_workaround: Developers construct custom message payloads using raw protocol buffers or use alternative channels like email for product sharing.
consequence: Limited marketing capabilities, manual workaround for product sharing, and inability to use WhatsApp's native business features.

workflow: Continuously updating and patching unofficial WhatsApp libraries to keep them working after WhatsApp changes the protocol.
trigger: WhatsApp rolling out updates that break existing library functionality.
current_workaround: Maintainers and community contributors manually reverse-engineer protocol changes, update code, and release patches. Users monitor issue trackers for fixes.
consequence: High maintenance burden on open-source maintainers, delayed fixes causing downtime for businesses, and risk of library abandonment.

workflow: Manually handling multi-device synchronization issues where messages are not delivered to all linked devices or sessions get out of sync.
trigger: WhatsApp's multi-device protocol not reliably syncing message state across all devices.
current_workaround: Developers implement custom sync logic, periodically re-authenticate devices, or limit automation to a single device.
consequence: Missed messages, duplicate message handling, and inconsistent state across devices leading to customer confusion.

workflow: Implementing custom media handling (sending/receiving images, videos, documents) because unofficial libraries have inconsistent support for media types and sizes.
trigger: Business need to send or receive media files through automation.
current_workaround: Developers write custom media encoding/decoding logic, handle upload/download manually, and implement retry mechanisms for failed media transfers.
consequence: Failed media transfers, corrupted files, and inability to support rich media communication in automated workflows.

workflow: Manually handling message queuing and delivery guarantees because unofficial libraries do not provide built-in retry or queue management.
trigger: Network issues, rate limiting, or temporary WhatsApp outages causing message delivery failures.
current_workaround: Developers implement custom message queues, database-backed retry logic, and delivery confirmation tracking.
consequence: Lost messages, duplicate sends, and unreliable automation requiring constant monitoring and manual intervention.

workflow: Implementing end-to-end encryption handling manually because unofficial libraries require custom decryption of incoming messages.
trigger: WhatsApp's encryption protocol changes or library updates breaking decryption logic.
current_workaround: Developers maintain custom encryption/decryption code, monitor library updates for breaking changes, and test message handling after each update.
consequence: Inability to read incoming messages, security vulnerabilities, and extra development effort to maintain encryption compatibility.
